findings.note: All three Block-after-rollback paths ignore `_discard_batch` returning false (lines 3454, 3484, and 3515). If the journal unlink fails after a completed rollback and durable Block Evidence write, `_discard_batch` has already removed `pre/`, the publication artifacts are at PRE, and Evidence contains the new Block record, which normally matches neither the journal's PRE nor POST hash. The next mandatory recovery scan therefore does not retry the discard as the implementation report claims; it classifies Evidence as a third state, emits `publication-journal-recovery`, and retains the journal for manual intervention. Thus an ordinary transient cleanup failure converts an otherwise completed, recoverable rollback into a permanently unrecoverable batch, contrary to the transactional completion/recovery contract. This is not attacker-controlled journal manipulation and falls outside owner ruling (c).
